text: 1d How do you make payroll, a famously tedious part of running a company, feel intelligent, seamless, and even beautiful? That was the challenge for the team building Mercury Payroll, which launched this week. For something nearly every founder eventually has to figure out, payroll has a way of becoming an enormous time and energy suck. A raise halfway through the month, a changing start date, or a new pay schedule can turn into hours of paperwork and calculations. One of the first questions the team asked was: If someone already uses Mercury, how quickly can we get them to the point where they're paying themselves or their team? For designer Alden H. and engineer Jordan Matyiku Nuñez, both on the Payroll team, the answer involved rethinking much more than the interface. As Jordan put it, “A lot of this was keeping payroll working while changing everything around it.” To make it intelligent, the team built automations that keep recurring payroll moving, flag potential issues before a pay run fails, and let founders use Command to handle unexpected changes, like adding a bonus, by just asking. To make it seamless, they redesigned onboarding around information Mercury already knows. Even selecting an account during setup, a seemingly effortless click, required intricate engineering to connect the systems behind the scenes. And to make it beautiful, they rebuilt the customer-facing experience from scratch. An early version of the pay run screen resembled an editable spreadsheet.
